learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the intense moral conflict between patriotism (duty to one's country) and professional ethics/human compassion (a doctor's duty to save lives).

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Dr. Sadao Hoki, a famous Japanese surgeon, and his wife Hana find a badly wounded, unconscious American Prisoner of War (Tom) washed ashore near their house during World War II.
If Sadao shelters the white man, he could be arrested as a traitor. If he turns him over to the police, the man will surely die. Sadao's medical ethics compel him to save the life.
Sadao operates and saves Tom, with Hana helping to give anesthesia despite her intense disgust. The servants, feeling Sadao is being unpatriotic, refuse to help and leave the house.

Sadao confesses to the old, sick General. The General promises to send private assassins to kill Tom silently. However, the General is so absorbed in his own pain that he completely forgets to send them.

Tired of waiting for the assassins and wanting the man out of his house, Sadao secretly helps Tom escape on a boat to a nearby island with food, water, and a flashlight. Sadao fulfills his duty as a doctor and a human.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Morality Scale
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are a doctor and your worst personal enemy is brought to you bleeding. Do you save them or let them perish? Write a one-sentence justification for your choice!

exam_tips: 📌 Focus on Hana's character: She is deeply prejudiced against Americans, yet she washes the man and helps in the surgery out of human dignity and loyalty to her husband.
📌 Why wasn't Sadao sent abroad with the troops? Because the old General might need surgery at any time, and he only trusted Sadao.
📌 The ending ('I wonder why I could not kill him?') shows that basic human goodness and professional ethics ultimately conquer national prejudice.
quick_recap: ⭐ Sadao and Hana met in America, but Sadao waited to fall in love until he was sure she was purely Japanese, respecting his traditional father.
⭐ The servants (Yumi, the gardener, the cook) represent the fierce, unquestioning patriotism of the general public.
⭐ Sadao instructed the POW to flash his light twice if he ran out of food, and once if he was okay.
